predictions: The T>C change has no TF-mediated effect; the association could reflect linkage or a mechanism not mediated by TF binding at this base.

chains.title: Candidate JUN-dependent regulation of FTO
chains.element: The variant overlaps a distal enhancer-like cCRE; whether it is active in the proposed cell type is unknown.

links.claim: JUN is a testable candidate because it has a peak over the variant in HepG2 and is the most highly expressed of the listed peak-overlapping TFs in the adipose proxy; neither establishes occupancy in preadipocytes. No QBiC-SELEX result or allele-specific binding direction is provided. Alt C is a provisional hypothesis, not an evidence-supported direction.
The variant lies in a distal enhancer-like cCRE, but activity in preadipocytes and an allele-dependent effect are not established.

FTO is the leading candidate target by credible-set L2G, but regulation of FTO by this cCRE is not demonstrated; the reported FTO eQTL is in skeletal muscle and no adipose-subcutaneous eQTL is reported.
Adipose-derived preadipocytes are a proposed context based on the expression proxy, not a demonstrated site of JUN occupancy at this variant.
The variant is strongly associated with obesity-related traits, but the association does not establish a JUN–cCRE–FTO mechanism or its regulatory direction.

predictions: In relevant preadipocytes, this provisional model predicts greater JUN binding to alt C than ref T and a JUN-dependent allele-specific regulatory effect; the direction of the downstream effect is unknown.
Unlike H4, this model predicts that disrupting JUN, rather than USF2, removes the allele-dependent effect.
falsified_if: JUN does not occupy the site in relevant cells, or a well-powered assay finds no JUN-dependent allele effect on regulatory output.

checks.why: Would test whether the current cross-cell-line JUN overlap has a corresponding peak in the closest available adipose biosample; it would not by itself establish allele-specific binding.
Would test whether the variant is associated with expression of FTO or another candidate target in the proposed tissue context.
Would assess whether independent gene-disease evidence supports RPGRIP1L as an obesity-related target, the weakest proposed target-gene choice.

matrix.test: Dual-allele enhancer reporter in adipose precursor cells, with control versus JUN or USF2 depletion; test for an allele-by-TF interaction.

outcomes.outcome: No reproducible allele-dependent reporter effect, or no effect specifically dependent on JUN or USF2.
An allele-dependent reporter effect that is reduced by JUN depletion; this model provisionally predicts greater binding for alt C, but the downstream direction is unknown.
An allele-dependent reporter effect that is reduced by USF2 depletion; this model provisionally predicts greater binding for alt C, but the downstream direction is unknown.

matrix.test: Check ENCODE or other available ChIP-seq data for a JUN peak in the closest available adipose-subcutaneous biosample.

outcomes.outcome: No matching peak is compatible with the null; a peak alone would not establish an allelic effect.
A matching peak would support occupancy in that biosample, but would not establish allele-specific binding.
A JUN peak is not required by this USF2 model and would not establish USF2-mediated allelic regulation.

matrix.test: Look up variant-associated expression of FTO and other candidate genes in GTEx Adipose - Subcutaneous.

outcomes.outcome: No adipose eQTL is compatible with the null; a detected eQTL alone would not prove TF mediation.
An FTO eQTL would be compatible with the proposed target, though not specific to JUN; absence would not by itself exclude a context-specific effect.
An FTO eQTL would be compatible with the proposed target, though not specific to USF2; absence would not by itself exclude a context-specific effect.

matrix.test: Check independent gene-disease evidence for RPGRIP1L and obesity.

outcomes.outcome: Any RPGRIP1L-disease association would not establish a TF-mediated effect of this variant.
RPGRIP1L evidence would not test the proposed JUN–FTO chain.
RPGRIP1L evidence would not test the proposed USF2–FTO chain.

next_experiment: The cheapest direct discriminator for the top two hypotheses (H1 and H2) is a dual-allele enhancer reporter in an adipose precursor cell model with control versus JUN depletion. H2 predicts a JUN-dependent allelic difference; H1 predicts no reproducible JUN-dependent allelic difference. The result would test the proposed mechanism, not prove endogenous regulation at the native locus.

Fat mass and obesity-associated (FTO) protein, an m6A demethylase involved in metabolic regulation, has been linked to obesity.

This narrative review aims to clarify the tissue-specific effects of the fat mass and obesity-associated (FTO) gene, which encodes a demethylase enzyme, on lipid and glucose metabolism and appetite regulation.
Mogroside V (MV) is a triterpene glycoside extracted from Siraitia grosvenorii and has shown beneficial effects in models of obesity.
MV promoted brown adipocyte thermogenesis through the FTO-m6A-LETMD1-UCP1 axis, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for obesity.
Single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs) in the FTO (rs[masked]) and melanocortin-4-receptor (MC4R) (rs[masked]) genes have been strongly linked to an increased risk of obesity.
This study shows a clear correlation between the higher incidence of obesity in Quetta, Pakistan, and the FTO rs[masked] and MC4R rs[masked] polymorphisms.
Variants in the FTO (fat mass and obesity-associated) gene are well established as genetic determinants of adiposity and metabolic dysfunction.
The BRI is a strong predictor of MASLD, with FTO risk allele further amplifying susceptibility to MASLD.

The fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) is an obesity-related protein that is widely expressed in different tissues throughout the human body, with relatively high expression levels observed in the brain.
Initial investigations into FTO mainly concentrated on its involvement in the development of obesity and diabetes.
